summary: First iteration full test of Anjali Herbal Life Ayurveda MVP. Ran 28 pytest backend API tests (all passing) covering health, public settings, product seed, admin login/CRUD/settings/reports/audit, OTP registration flow with dev_otp, distributor_id generation (ANJxxxxxx), duplicate email + invalid OTP + invalid sponsor rejection, order creation with 5% GST + Stripe checkout URL, RED-user withdrawal restriction, KYC submit with masking, admin KYC verify, authorization (403 for distributor on /admin, 401 without token). Ran a Playwright UI test verifying landing loads, language switcher works, admin login redirects to /admin, all 9 admin sub-pages render, 2-step registration with OTP auto-fill lands on /app/dashboard with RED 'Activate Now' banner, referral page shows ANJ id, products page shows Starter Kit. Stripe checkout completion + GREEN activation + ₹100 referral commission credit cannot be fully automated (requires interactive card entry on the hosted Stripe page); code review of _process_paid_order confirms idempotency via double-guard (order.payment_status $ne paid, referral.commission_paid $ne True, and existing-commission check).

issues: Recharts warning: width(-1)/height(-1) on income chart container on first render — harmless but should set explicit minHeight or use ResponsiveContainer aspect prop

action_items: MANUAL/BROWSER TEST NEEDED: Full end-to-end payment flow with Stripe test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 — verify (a) order becomes paid + invoice_number set, (b) user becomes GREEN, (c) sponsor gets exactly ₹100 REFERRAL_COMMISSION when a GREEN-referred user activates, (d) polling status multiple times does not create duplicate commissions. Backend logic is well-guarded but cannot be verified without an actual paid Stripe session.
Minor: fix Recharts container size warning on dashboard income chart (set minHeight on ResponsiveContainer wrapper).
critical_code_review_comments: shop_routes._process_paid_order is well-designed: uses conditional Mongo update ({payment_status: {$ne: 'paid'}}) + rel.commission_paid guard + commissions uniqueness check → idempotent under repeated polling. Good.
shop_routes.payment_status endpoint finalizes on poll (webhook-independent) which is correct for preview environment.

auth_routes.login has brute-force lockout at 5 attempts (429). Good. However lockout has no auto-expiry; a stuck login_attempts row will block a user permanently. Consider adding a time-based reset (e.g., after 10 min).

wallet_routes.request_withdrawal calls add_wallet_transaction with status='DEBITED' (which deducts available_balance) AND then 'PENDING' (which increments pending_balance). On mark_paid it decrements pending_balance and adds a REVERSED debit txn. Math is consistent, but the double-txn pattern is a bit confusing — consider a single atomic 'HOLD' status for readability.
core.hash_password uses bcrypt.gensalt() (default rounds) → produces $2b$ hash. Verified format via test flow.
CORS is allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False → OK since auth is Bearer-token, not cookies.
No _id leakage: all find queries project {_id: 0} or use clean_user helper. Verified across routes.
auth_routes.send_otp deletes any previous OTP for the email — good; prevents stale OTPs.
server.py seed_admin correctly re-hashes password if the env-provided admin password doesn't match existing hash — playbook-compliant.
shop_routes.create_checkout uses server-side order.total (never client-supplied amount) → prevents payment tampering. Good.
Missing rate limit on /api/auth/send-otp — could be spammed to enumerate/annoy. Non-blocking for MVP but flag for phase 2.
No pagination on list endpoints (products, orders, admin/*). Fine for MVP scale but will need pagination for production.
